Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

4	
5	fast-ulysses 的 README 里有一堆数字——1.60–2.17× 于 `torch.distributed` 路径、传输达 fabric 上限 90–99%、hidden% 等。本讲要回答的问题是：**这些数字是怎么测出来的，以及为什么这样测才可信**。学完本讲，你应该能够：
6	
7	1. 对 `benchmark/bench_a2a.py` 的七种模式各写出一句话的问题定义与判读方法，重点掌握 stages 分解中每一列回答什么问题。

9	3. 复述 zerosm A/B 的双列联读法，以及代码里为让这两列可信所付出的全部设计代价。
10	4. 说明独占执行（EXCLUSIVE/CONTENDED）为何是一切数字有效的前提，并掌握 `tools/exclusive.sh` 的三段式工作流。
11	
12	## 2. 前置知识
13	
14	- **CUDA 事件计时 vs 主机墙钟**：`torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)` 在流上打时间戳，度量的是设备侧两件事之间的时间；`time.perf_counter()` 度量的是主机提交代码的耗时。二者回答不同问题——本讲会看到两个都用的地方。
15	- **中位数与预热**：GPU 上首次调用含缓存分配、JIT、驱动懒初始化等一次性成本，所以每次测量都先 warmup 再取多次运行的中位数（对离群邻居干扰更稳）。
16	- **集合通信的计时要对齐 rank**：一次 all-to-all 的耗时由最慢的 rank 决定。若各 rank 的 warmup 次数不同，一个 rank 的预热残留会落进另一个 rank 的计时窗口，故计时前要 `dist.barrier()`。
17	- **共享 GPU 与邻居进程**：基准机往往是共享的，任务随时到来。邻居进程占用 SM、带宽、还会让 SM 时钟掉频——这些都不受你控制，却全部落进你的计时窗口。
18	- **fabric 带宽**：NVLink 互联（fabric）能搬运的每秒字节数有物理上限。「用了 fabric 的百分之多少」是判断「还有没有调度空间」的判据。
19	- **承接前讲**：u6-l2 讲过一次调用是「prepare 校验 → 开路屏障 → CE 传输 → 收尾屏障 → copy_out」五段；u5-l2 讲过零 SM 仅属跨链路远端拷贝、zerosm 用双臂 A/B 检验。本讲把这些性质变成**可测、可判读的数字**。

34	### 4.1 stages 分解：一次调用的时间去哪了

37	
38	stages 模式回答的问题是：**「两边各自的时间都花在哪了」**。它把两条路径各自拆成若干段，使各段**相加等于整个调用**，而不是仅仅与总和相关。这一点是整个 fast-ulysses 性能论证的地基：
39	
40	- BASE 是 sglang `usp.py` 的路径：permute → `all_to_all_single` → permute，拆成三段；

127	- **hidden%**：异步调用在并发 GEMM 下消失的份额。定义：
128	  \[ \text{hidden\%} = \frac{t_{\text{serial}} - t_{\text{concurrent}}}{t_{\text{a2a,alone}}} \times 100\% \]

192	### 4.3 zerosm A/B：一次只差一个变量的实验
193	
194	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
195	
196	zerosm 模式回答：**「一次拷贝到底占不占 SM」**。u5-l2 已建立判读法——GEMM 慢化与成对比（pair ratio）**两列联读**：`1.00× 慢化 + 1.00× 成对比` 才是零 SM；`1.00× 慢化 + 成对比贴满完全竞争参照` 则是拷贝被 GEMM 饿死。本讲从「怎么让这两列可信」的角度精读实验装置本身，它有三个原则：
197	
198	1. **两臂只差一个变量**：peer 臂（目的在对端的对称内存窗口，拷贝过链路）vs same 臂（目的是本 rank 自己的内存）——同样的字节、同样的 `dst.copy_(src)` 调用。
199	2. **绕开本算子**：算子路径自带两个屏障内核和一个 copy-out，它们**按构造就是 SM 工作**，整调用测出的任何东西都无法归因给传输。
200	3. **每臂配自己的 GEMM 链**：同样字节到 peer 和到本地内存耗时不同（差数倍），共享一条链会让较短的那臂（same 臂——正是应该显出慢化的臂）被拉向 1.00×，实验就瞎了。
201	
202	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
203	
204	对两个 payload（设计工作点的字节数、64 MiB）× 两种流数（单流：仅 rank 0 动；ws 流：全员各写邻座）：
205	
206	1. **拷贝次数校准**：对每臂单测一次单拷贝时长，取最快臂为基准，把拷贝重复次数 `creps` 定到「最短臂也至少持续 LONG_MS = 20 ms」；由 rank 0 算出后 `dist.broadcast`——每个 rank 必须发出相同的工作。
207	2. **每臂链长校准**：再单测每臂 creps 次拷贝的时长，链上 GEMM 个数 = 该时长 / 单个 GEMM 时长（取整、至少 1），同样广播。
208	3. **交替采样**：ROUNDS=5 轮 × 每轮内两臂交替；臂内「并发区」与它作除数的两个 alone 测量也交替。注释说明：若基线只在开头测一次，整轮漂移会全部灌进慢化列。`dist.barrier` 保证各 rank 同处一臂——这是「ws 流行真是 ws 流测量」的前提。
209	4. **并发区构造**（`pair()`）：先入队 GEMM 链再入队拷贝——链是几次 launch、拷贝是几百次，后入队的会晚起跑，先入队链把这段暴露压到最小；在链后打一个 mark，把「链自身在并发区内的时长」单独读出。
210	5. 每臂输出四列：copy（单独）、gemm（链单独）、pair（并发区墙钟）、gemm slowdown（链在并发区内时长 / 链单独时长），外加 pair ratio 与 full comp 两个派生。
211	
212	判读用的两个派生量：
213	\[ \text{pair ratio} = \frac{t_{\text{pair}}}{\max(t_{\text{copy}},\ t_{\text{gemm}})}, \qquad \text{full comp} = \frac{t_{\text{copy}} + t_{\text{gemm}}}{\max(t_{\text{copy}},\ t_{\text{gemm}})} \]

264	### 4.4 独占执行纪律：exclusive.sh 的三段式
265	
266	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
267	
268	`bench_a2a.py` 模块 docstring 第一句就是纪律：「**在 tools/exclusive.sh 下运行——来自共享 GPU 的数字不是数字**」（L3–5）。为什么：
269	
270	1. **邻居负载是随机变量**：共享机上任务不请自来，30 秒前空闲的 GPU 现在就可能有人；干扰直接落进计时窗口，结果「看起来像真实测量——只是是错的」。
271	2. **部分竞争不可见**：4 个 rank 里 2 个被邻居拖慢，集合通信的耗时由最慢 rank 决定，整个数字被抬高，而输出里**没有任何痕迹**指明原因（exclusive.sh 头注释 L5–8）。
272	3. **掉频是第二个混杂**：邻居负载会压低 SM 时钟，所有 SM 工作（GEMM、permute、屏障内核）整体变慢，比例失真——所以采样器还记录最低 SM 时钟。
273	
274	因此脚本的工作流是三段式：**等空闲 → 边跑边采样 → 判决**，判决只有两种：EXCLUSIVE（数字可用）或 CONTENDED（**丢弃这些数字**，退出码 4）。
275	
276	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
277	
278	1. **等空闲**：`foreign_count` 用 `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` 按 GPU UUID 数出请求的每张卡上的进程数；非零则每 10 秒重试，超过 `WAIT_SECS`（默认 0）则 `REFUSED` 退出——「不在共享 GPU 上测量」。
279	2. **边跑边采样**：后台每 `SAMPLE_SECS`（默认 5 秒）记录一次「进程数 + 请求卡集中的最低 SM 时钟」；采样器监视父进程存活，父亡则止——孤儿采样器会在下一次运行里被当成「外来进程」。`trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM HUP` 保证断连时杀掉采样器并删临时文件。
280	3. **绑定设备**：`export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${DEVICES}"`——不绑定的话「脚本监视一组设备而运行落在另一组」（torch 默认用 0..N-1），一个 EXCLUSIVE 判决就对数字的出处一言不发。
281	4. **判决**：整个运行期间见过的最大进程数 `max_seen` 若超过 `expected = GPU 数 × EXPECT_PER_GPU`（默认 1，即每卡一个进程是我们自己的贡献，多出来的都是邻居）→ `CONTENDED`；否则 `EXCLUSIVE`，附样本数、最大进程数、最低 SM 时钟。

330	### 4.5 可归因的数字：collect.sh 与 benchmark.md 的方法纪律
331	
332	#### 4.5.1 概念说明
333	
334	一个基准数字的价值等于它的**可归因性**（attribution）：知道它来自哪台机器、哪个 commit、哪个构建、哪套环境，数字才能被复现、被比较、被撤回。`collect.sh` 的头注释说得直接：「同型号 GPU 的两个节点可以相差超过被测的任何东西，而这只有当每个数字都说清自己来自哪台机器、哪个构建、哪个 commit 时才可捕捉」。它把一次完整测量组织成：
335	
336	1. **指纹头**：任何数字之前先记录环境——日期、主机名、GPU 列表、仓库、commit、驱动、torch/CUDA 版本、GPU 型号与数量、fast_ulysses 版本与构建信息、测量前的 SM 时钟/温度/功率上限、`nvidia-smi topo -m` 拓扑、`doctor` 输出。
337	2. **正确性门**：先跑 `pytest test/`，「来自一个连自己的测试都过不了的构建的数字比没有数字更糟，因为它看起来像数据」。失败则整个流程终止，一个测量都不做。
338	3. **全部模式依次过 exclusive.sh**：顺序 stages → zerocopy → sweep → link → zerosm → overlap → padding，全部包在 `tools/exclusive.sh` 里；GPU ≥ 4 时追加 `stages` 的 ws=4 一遍（切分形状随 world size 变化）。
339	4. **失败清算**：用 `PIPESTATUS[0]` 取运行自身的退出码（而非管道的），失败的模式记名，结尾打印 `INCOMPLETE` 与「在解释清楚之前不要从中发表任何东西」。
340	
341	`docs/benchmark.md` 再补三条发表纪律：**单一 wheel**（同一 sha256 的二进制装到所有机器，跨代际之间不重编译）、**每型号两台机器**（两台一致才展示一台并注明展布；不一致则两台都列、绝不平均——v0.1 曾因第二台同型号机器差 5× 而撤回已发表的一行）、**未测量就声明未测量**（0.2.1 新增的暂存池与 lend 无数字；zerosm 写于测量之后故无表）。
342

344	
345	`collect.sh <label> [gpu-list]` 的执行流：

347	```
348	tee 到 ${OUTDIR}/${LABEL}.log
349	├── 指纹头（date/host/gpus/repo/commit/driver/torch/GPU/版本）
350	├── clocks(before) + topo -m + fast-ulysses doctor
351	├── 正确性门：pytest test/ ──失败──→ "GATE FAILED"，exit 1
352	├── for mode in stages zerocopy sweep link zerosm overlap padding:

354	│      （PIPESTATUS 记失败模式名）
355	├── NPROC ≥ 4 时再跑一遍 stages@4
356	├── clocks(after)

417	4. **写判读笔记**：回答——两节点展布落在屏障（到达偏斜）而非传输时，说明什么？（答：被搬的东西没变，偏斜只是挪到了两道握手之间，见 `docs/benchmark.md` L89–L91。）CONTENDED 的运行能靠「多跑几遍取中位数」补救吗？（答：不能——干扰是时变且不对称的，中位数只能抵抗离群值，不能移除系统性抬升；且你无法事后分辨哪个数字被污染。）
418	
419	无 GPU 时第 2 步写为纸面方案并标注「待本地验证」；第 1、3、4 步全部可离线完成（本文 4.1.4、4.2.4 已给出可对答案的样例）。
420	
421	## 6. 本讲小结
422	
423	- **stages 分解**让各段时间相加等于整个调用：BASE 三段、OURS 四段；`a2a` 对 `transfer` 是 like-for-like，`raw` 是传输下界而非替代方案；`relayout%`、`copyout%`、`raw/CE` 三个归一化列把「快」拆成可归因的命题。
424	- **两个归一化指标**：`hidden% = (serial − concurrent)/a2a_alone` 度量异步调用藏进计算的份额（有真实展布，当区间读，且受可用计算量约束）；`of the fabric = 过链路字节/transfer ÷ 单流上限` 度量调度剩余空间（90–99% 即无事可调度），上限由绕开本算子的 link 模式独立建立。
425	- **zerosm A/B** 的可信度来自装置：两臂只差目的地、绕开算子（屏障与 copy-out 按构造是 SM 工作）、每臂配自己等长的链、拷贝次数按最快臂校准并广播、臂与基线全部交替采样；判读必须**双列联读**——单看 gemm slowdown 无法区分「零 SM」与「被饿死」。
426	- **独占执行是前提**：共享 GPU 上的邻居负载是时变、不对称、且在输出中不可见的混杂；`exclusive.sh` 三段式（等空闲 → 边跑边采样进程数与最低 SM 时钟 → EXCLUSIVE/CONTENDED 判决）把「数字是否有效」变成显式输出；CONTENDED 的数字丢弃而非补救。
427	- **可归因性**：`collect.sh` 的指纹头（含 commit 的三层回退与 UNKNOWN 即禁发表）、正确性门、PIPESTATUS 失败记账，加上 benchmark.md 的单一 wheel、每型号两台、不一致就都列不平均、未测量就声明未测量——共同保证数字可复现、可比较、可撤回。
428	- 基准的每个模式是一个**问题**而不是一个数字：stages 问时间去哪了、overlap 问藏了多少、padding/zerocopy 问两条特性路径的代价、sweep 问何时失效、link 问天花板在哪、zerosm 问占不占 SM。
429	
430	## 7. 下一步学习建议
431	
432	- 下一讲 **u9-l5（设计反思）**：把本讲的实测证据接到 `docs/design.md` 的假设复盘上——CE 写入可见性假设、为何拒绝 PCIe（本讲 PCIe 一节的两台 5× 分歧正是论据）、被移除的方案表。
433	- 继续阅读源码：`benchmark/bench_a2a.py` 的 `run_padding`（L262–L306）与 `_baseline_unpadded`（L309–L324）——「对照必须测同一件事」的又一范例（不能拿两个不同的基线互比）；以及 `docs/benchmark.md` 的 "Alternatives tried and not adopted" 一表，每行都是一个被测量否决的设计。

# 基准方法论：stages/overlap/zerosm 与独占执行

## 1. 本讲目标

fast-ulysses 的 README 里有一堆数字——1.60–2.17× 于 `torch.distributed` 路径、传输达 fabric 上限 90–99%、hidden% 等。本讲要回答的问题是：**这些数字是怎么测出来的，以及为什么这样测才可信**。学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 对 `benchmark/bench_a2a.py` 的七种模式各写出一句话的问题定义与判读方法，重点掌握 stages 分解中每一列回答什么问题。
2. 解释 `hidden%` 与 `of the fabric` 两个归一化指标的定义、分子分母各自量的是什么。
3. 复述 zerosm A/B 的双列联读法，以及代码里为让这两列可信所付出的全部设计代价。
4. 说明独占执行（EXCLUSIVE/CONTENDED）为何是一切数字有效的前提，并掌握 `tools/exclusive.sh` 的三段式工作流。

## 2. 前置知识

- **CUDA 事件计时 vs 主机墙钟**：`torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)` 在流上打时间戳，度量的是设备侧两件事之间的时间；`time.perf_counter()` 度量的是主机提交代码的耗时。二者回答不同问题——本讲会看到两个都用的地方。
- **中位数与预热**：GPU 上首次调用含缓存分配、JIT、驱动懒初始化等一次性成本，所以每次测量都先 warmup 再取多次运行的中位数（对离群邻居干扰更稳）。
- **集合通信的计时要对齐 rank**：一次 all-to-all 的耗时由最慢的 rank 决定。若各 rank 的 warmup 次数不同，一个 rank 的预热残留会落进另一个 rank 的计时窗口，故计时前要 `dist.barrier()`。
- **共享 GPU 与邻居进程**：基准机往往是共享的，任务随时到来。邻居进程占用 SM、带宽、还会让 SM 时钟掉频——这些都不受你控制，却全部落进你的计时窗口。
- **fabric 带宽**：NVLink 互联（fabric）能搬运的每秒字节数有物理上限。「用了 fabric 的百分之多少」是判断「还有没有调度空间」的判据。
- **承接前讲**：u6-l2 讲过一次调用是「prepare 校验 → 开路屏障 → CE 传输 → 收尾屏障 → copy_out」五段；u5-l2 讲过零 SM 仅属跨链路远端拷贝、zerosm 用双臂 A/B 检验。本讲把这些性质变成**可测、可判读的数字**。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 行数 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `benchmark/bench_a2a.py` | 681 | 七种测量模式的主脚本；模块 docstring 本身就是一份判读手册 |
| `tools/exclusive.sh` | 113 | 独占执行守门人：等空闲 → 边跑边采样 → 打出 EXCLUSIVE/CONTENDED 判决 |
| `benchmark/collect.sh` | 139 | 一台机器的完整测量流程：指纹头 → 正确性门 → 依次跑全部模式 |
| `docs/benchmark.md` | 336 | 已发表数字与全部方法论纪律（两台机器、单一 wheel、撤回记录、未测量清单） |
| `python/fast_ulysses/group.py` | — | `_timed()`：基准专用的分段计时探针（L251–L265） |
| `src/bindings.cc` | — | `all_to_all_4d_timed` 算子：在四段之间记录 CUDA 事件（L624–L654） |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 stages 分解：一次调用的时间去哪了

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

stages 模式回答的问题是：**「两边各自的时间都花在哪了」**。它把两条路径各自拆成若干段，使各段**相加等于整个调用**，而不是仅仅与总和相关。这一点是整个 fast-ulysses 性能论证的地基：

- BASE 是 sglang `usp.py` 的路径：permute → `all_to_all_single` → permute，拆成三段；
- OURS 是本库的调用，拆成四段：`barr_in / transfer / barr_out / copy_out`（transfer 里含本 rank 自份额）；
- 另测一个 `raw`：单独跑平坦的 `all_to_all_single`——同样的字节数、不做任何重排、结果是错误布局，所以它是**传输下界**，不是可选方案。

拆段之后，「基线的重排内核占了多少」「我们的握手占了多少」从猜测变成算术。模块 docstring 说得很直白：`a2a` 对 `transfer` 是同类项对比（like-for-like pair），其余各段是每条路径围绕它必须多付的——「这整个就是论证本身，因为基线的重排是 SM 工作，会和这个设计想要藏身的计算相竞争」。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

`run_stages` 对 `SHAPES` 里每个真实模型形状（wan-720p / wan-480p / h3-t2va-5s）执行：

1. 头数不能整除 world_size 则跳过该形状（mode 0 散射头轴）。
2. `s_total` 向下取整到 ws 的倍数——这是基线需要的「padded shard」。
3. 分配输入 `x` 与等长的平坦 `send`/`recv`。
4. `base = median_of(baseline_stages(...))` → 基线三段的中位数。
5. `ours = median_of(group._timed(...))` → 本库四段的中位数。
6. `raw = median_ms(all_to_all_single(recv, send))` → 平坦传输下界。
7. `submit = submit_us(...)` → 主机提交一次同步调用的微秒数。
8. rank 0 打印一行，`dist.barrier()` 对齐后进入下一形状。

计时基建的三个关键设计：

- **Stopwatch**：CUDA 事件只在流上按序记录，最后一次读出相邻事件差。打点花的是主机时间、不占设备时间，所以「细分过的运行测出的总和与不细分的相同」。
- **median_of**：对每次运行收集各段耗时列表，再**对每个段位独立取中位数**。注意一个细节：表中 BASE/OURS 总计是各段中位数之和，不是「总时的中位数」——各段无交叠、无空隙（同一条流上严格排序），所以任何时间都被归因到某一段。
- **median_ms**：预热后先 `dist.barrier()` 再计时（对齐各 rank 起跑线）；**baseline_stages 只在 run_stages 里用**，因为它的 `read()` 会主机同步，落进任何外层计时区都会污染测量。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

计时的底层是基准专用算子：[python/fast_ulysses/group.py:L251-L265](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L251-L265)——`_timed()` 调用 `all_to_all_4d_timed` 算子，把返回的四个数贴上 `("barrier_in", "transfer", "barrier_out", "copy_out")` 的名字。docstring 明说「各段之和等于整个调用，因为它们在一条流上严格有序；读事件会同步」。

事件打在哪里：[src/bindings.cc:L624-L654](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/bindings.cc#L624-L654)——五个事件把复制路径（`prepare(..., std::nullopt, kSyncWindow, lend=false)`，即不带 out= 的普通调用）切成四段：`fast_barrier` → `launch_a2a_ce` → `fast_barrier` → `copy_out`，与 u6-l2 的流水线一一对应。注释特意说明事件用默认标志（不禁用计时），因为 `cudaEventElapsedTime` 需要时间戳。

Stopwatch 与三个中位数工具：[benchmark/bench_a2a.py:L84-L137](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/benchmark/bench_a2a.py#L84-L137)——`Stopwatch.mark()` 只记录事件、`read()` 在末尾统一读出差值；`median_of` 按段位取中位数；`median_ms` 在预热后加 `dist.barrier()`；`submit_us` 用 `perf_counter` 测主机提交耗时（批折叠要压平的正是这个量）。

基线的两种形态：[benchmark/bench_a2a.py:L140-L165](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/benchmark/bench_a2a.py#L140-L165)——`baseline_padded` 无插桩（可被整体计时），`baseline_stages` 在三段间打事件。注意 L153–L154 的 docstring：`read()` 会主机同步，故仅 `run_stages` 使用。

主表与全部派生列：[benchmark/bench_a2a.py:L168-L214](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/benchmark/bench_a2a.py#L168-L214)——表头在 L175–L181，四组测量在 L197–L202，打印在 L204–L213。三个派生列的计算就在打印行里：

- `raw/CE = raw / ours[1]`（L209）——平坦 `all_to_all_single` 除以本库 transfer 段；
- `relayout% = (base[0] + base[2]) / base_total`（L210）——基线两个 permute 占其总时间的份额；
- `copyout% = ours[3] / ours_total`（L211）——copy_out 占本库总时间的份额。

**读表陷阱**：表中的 `a2a` 列是**基线的** `all_to_all_single` 段，不是本库调用；本库的对应列叫 `transfer`。这一对才是 like-for-like。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：为 stages 输出的每一列写一行判读模板，并用 `docs/benchmark.md` 已发表的一行数字手工验证派生列的算术。

**操作步骤**：

1. 精读 [benchmark/bench_a2a.py:L10-L16](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/benchmark/bench_a2a.py#L10-L16)（stages 模式 docstring）与 L175–L181 的表头。
2. 抄下 `docs/benchmark.md` H200 行（wan-720p）：perm_in 0.358、a2a 0.826、perm_out 0.385、BASE 1.569、transfer 0.680、copy_out 0.143、OURS 0.860、raw 0.859。
3. 手工复算三个派生列并与表中 47.3%、1.26×、16.6% 对照。
4. 写出你的判读模板表（下面答案给出参考版）。

**需要观察的现象 / 预期结果**：

- `relayout% = (0.358 + 0.385) / 1.569 = 47.35% ≈ 47.3%` ✓
- `raw/CE = 0.859 / 0.680 = 1.263 ≈ 1.26×` ✓
- `copyout% = 0.143 / 0.860 = 16.6%` ✓（且与 benchmark.md 零拷贝表中 H200 wan-720p 的「copy_out 占计时各段 16.6%」互相印证）

三列全部对上即证明你对列语义的理解与代码一致。有 GPU 时可运行（待本地验证）：

```bash
./tools/exclusive.sh 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 -- torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 \
    benchmark/bench_a2a.py --mode stages
```

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`raw` 列为什么是「传输下界」而不是「替代方案」？

**答案**：`raw` 只跑平坦的 `all_to_all_single`，搬运同样的字节但完全不做重排，结果处于错误布局（L12–L14、L172–L174）。真实调用必须把数据放回正确布局，所以 raw 不是能用的路径；它只回答「光搬这些字节最少要多久」，用来给 transfer 列定标尺。

**练习 2**：`submit us` 列测的是什么？它想守住哪个设计？

**答案**：测主机提交一次调用的微秒数（`submit_us` 的 docstring，L126–L127）。CE 传输会把一次交换拆成许多条 `cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync`，若每条的提交开销在主机侧累积，卡就会饿。批折叠（把 batch 维折叠进 3D 拷贝）要压平的就是这个量——它跟设备侧时间无关。

**练习 3**：为什么 `median_of` 对每个段位独立取中位数，而不是先取每次运行的总和再取中位数？

**答案**：这里的目标是**归因**而非单点估计：每个段位的中位数对邻居干扰等离群值最稳，而各段在同一条流上无交叠、无空隙，段位中位数之和仍是总时间的一个稳健估计。两种算法给出的「总」可能略有差别，但归因结论（哪段占多少）不因这个选择翻转。

### 4.2 overlap 隐藏率与「of the fabric」：两个归一化指标

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

两个归一化指标把「快」翻译成可比较的命题：

- **hidden%**：异步调用在并发 GEMM 下消失的份额。定义：
  \[ \text{hidden\%} = \frac{t_{\text{serial}} - t_{\text{concurrent}}}{t_{\text{a2a,alone}}} \times 100\% \]
  分子是「先通信后计算」与「通信计算并发」的墙钟差，分母是通信自身单独跑的时间。这是零 SM 设计**存在意义**所系的命题（L18–20）。
- **of the fabric**：transfer 段实际用掉的 fabric 带宽占上限的百分比。上限由 link 模式独立测得——**绕开本算子**、直接用 torch 对称内存做平坦 64 MiB peer 拷贝，「让天花板独立于被审判的对象建立」（L42–L45）。

归一化的意义在于分离混杂因素：hidden% 把「GEMM 本身多慢」从分子分母中约掉；of-the-fabric 把「消息多大」约掉，只剩「调度还有没有空间」——80% 以上就没有什么可调度的了，30% 则有。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

**overlap 模式**（[benchmark/bench_a2a.py:L217-L259](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/benchmark/bench_a2a.py#L217-L259)）：

1. 用 `SHAPES[0]`（wan-720p），配三个 `a @ w`（k=n=5120）模拟 to_q/k/v 的形状。
2. 单独测 `t_gemm`、`t_a2a`。
3. `serial()` = 同步 a2a 然后 GEMM 链；`concurrent()` = `all_to_all_4d_async` + GEMM 链 + `wait()`。
4. **两种安排交替执行**各 8 轮、每轮内部再取 8 次的中位数，最后取轮间中位数——因为「GEMM 窗口逐轮漂移的幅度和 a2a 本身差不多，交替能抵消漂移」（L244–L245）。
5. 打印 hidden% 及两边的 min–max 展布。

**link 模式**（[benchmark/bench_a2a.py:L402-L443](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/benchmark/bench_a2a.py#L402-L443)）：

1. 经 `torch.distributed._symmetric_memory` 分配 64 MiB，rendezvous 后取 `(rank+1)%ws` 的窗口。
2. `one_pair`：只有 rank 0 拷贝 → fabric 上单一流；`all_pairs`：每 rank 都拷贝 → ws 条流。
3. 打印单流 GB/s 与聚合 GB/s，末尾说明判读方法：stages 的 `transfer` 除以**真正过链路的字节**（总量 × (ws−1)/ws），再除以单流上限，就是「用了 fabric 的百分之多少」。

### 4.3 zerosm A/B：一次只差一个变量的实验

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

zerosm 模式回答：**「一次拷贝到底占不占 SM」**。u5-l2 已建立判读法——GEMM 慢化与成对比（pair ratio）**两列联读**：`1.00× 慢化 + 1.00× 成对比` 才是零 SM；`1.00× 慢化 + 成对比贴满完全竞争参照` 则是拷贝被 GEMM 饿死。本讲从「怎么让这两列可信」的角度精读实验装置本身，它有三个原则：

1. **两臂只差一个变量**：peer 臂（目的在对端的对称内存窗口，拷贝过链路）vs same 臂（目的是本 rank 自己的内存）——同样的字节、同样的 `dst.copy_(src)` 调用。
2. **绕开本算子**：算子路径自带两个屏障内核和一个 copy-out，它们**按构造就是 SM 工作**，整调用测出的任何东西都无法归因给传输。
3. **每臂配自己的 GEMM 链**：同样字节到 peer 和到本地内存耗时不同（差数倍），共享一条链会让较短的那臂（same 臂——正是应该显出慢化的臂）被拉向 1.00×，实验就瞎了。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

对两个 payload（设计工作点的字节数、64 MiB）× 两种流数（单流：仅 rank 0 动；ws 流：全员各写邻座）：

1. **拷贝次数校准**：对每臂单测一次单拷贝时长，取最快臂为基准，把拷贝重复次数 `creps` 定到「最短臂也至少持续 LONG_MS = 20 ms」；由 rank 0 算出后 `dist.broadcast`——每个 rank 必须发出相同的工作。
2. **每臂链长校准**：再单测每臂 creps 次拷贝的时长，链上 GEMM 个数 = 该时长 / 单个 GEMM 时长（取整、至少 1），同样广播。
3. **交替采样**：ROUNDS=5 轮 × 每轮内两臂交替；臂内「并发区」与它作除数的两个 alone 测量也交替。注释说明：若基线只在开头测一次，整轮漂移会全部灌进慢化列。`dist.barrier` 保证各 rank 同处一臂——这是「ws 流行真是 ws 流测量」的前提。
4. **并发区构造**（`pair()`）：先入队 GEMM 链再入队拷贝——链是几次 launch、拷贝是几百次，后入队的会晚起跑，先入队链把这段暴露压到最小；在链后打一个 mark，把「链自身在并发区内的时长」单独读出。
5. 每臂输出四列：copy（单独）、gemm（链单独）、pair（并发区墙钟）、gemm slowdown（链在并发区内时长 / 链单独时长），外加 pair ratio 与 full comp 两个派生。

判读用的两个派生量：
\[ \text{pair ratio} = \frac{t_{\text{pair}}}{\max(t_{\text{copy}},\ t_{\text{gemm}})}, \qquad \text{full comp} = \frac{t_{\text{copy}} + t_{\text{gemm}}}{\max(t_{\text{copy}},\ t_{\text{gemm}})} \]

### 4.4 独占执行纪律：exclusive.sh 的三段式

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

`bench_a2a.py` 模块 docstring 第一句就是纪律：「**在 tools/exclusive.sh 下运行——来自共享 GPU 的数字不是数字**」（L3–5）。为什么：

1. **邻居负载是随机变量**：共享机上任务不请自来，30 秒前空闲的 GPU 现在就可能有人；干扰直接落进计时窗口，结果「看起来像真实测量——只是是错的」。
2. **部分竞争不可见**：4 个 rank 里 2 个被邻居拖慢，集合通信的耗时由最慢 rank 决定，整个数字被抬高，而输出里**没有任何痕迹**指明原因（exclusive.sh 头注释 L5–8）。
3. **掉频是第二个混杂**：邻居负载会压低 SM 时钟，所有 SM 工作（GEMM、permute、屏障内核）整体变慢，比例失真——所以采样器还记录最低 SM 时钟。

因此脚本的工作流是三段式：**等空闲 → 边跑边采样 → 判决**，判决只有两种：EXCLUSIVE（数字可用）或 CONTENDED（**丢弃这些数字**，退出码 4）。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

1. **等空闲**：`foreign_count` 用 `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` 按 GPU UUID 数出请求的每张卡上的进程数；非零则每 10 秒重试，超过 `WAIT_SECS`（默认 0）则 `REFUSED` 退出——「不在共享 GPU 上测量」。
2. **边跑边采样**：后台每 `SAMPLE_SECS`（默认 5 秒）记录一次「进程数 + 请求卡集中的最低 SM 时钟」；采样器监视父进程存活，父亡则止——孤儿采样器会在下一次运行里被当成「外来进程」。`trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM HUP` 保证断连时杀掉采样器并删临时文件。
3. **绑定设备**：`export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${DEVICES}"`——不绑定的话「脚本监视一组设备而运行落在另一组」（torch 默认用 0..N-1），一个 EXCLUSIVE 判决就对数字的出处一言不发。
4. **判决**：整个运行期间见过的最大进程数 `max_seen` 若超过 `expected = GPU 数 × EXPECT_PER_GPU`（默认 1，即每卡一个进程是我们自己的贡献，多出来的都是邻居）→ `CONTENDED`；否则 `EXCLUSIVE`，附样本数、最大进程数、最低 SM 时钟。

- **stages 分解**让各段时间相加等于整个调用：BASE 三段、OURS 四段；`a2a` 对 `transfer` 是 like-for-like，`raw` 是传输下界而非替代方案；`relayout%`、`copyout%`、`raw/CE` 三个归一化列把「快」拆成可归因的命题。
- **两个归一化指标**：`hidden% = (serial − concurrent)/a2a_alone` 度量异步调用藏进计算的份额（有真实展布，当区间读，且受可用计算量约束）；`of the fabric = 过链路字节/transfer ÷ 单流上限` 度量调度剩余空间（90–99% 即无事可调度），上限由绕开本算子的 link 模式独立建立。
- **zerosm A/B** 的可信度来自装置：两臂只差目的地、绕开算子（屏障与 copy-out 按构造是 SM 工作）、每臂配自己等长的链、拷贝次数按最快臂校准并广播、臂与基线全部交替采样；判读必须**双列联读**——单看 gemm slowdown 无法区分「零 SM」与「被饿死」。
- **独占执行是前提**：共享 GPU 上的邻居负载是时变、不对称、且在输出中不可见的混杂；`exclusive.sh` 三段式（等空闲 → 边跑边采样进程数与最低 SM 时钟 → EXCLUSIVE/CONTENDED 判决）把「数字是否有效」变成显式输出；CONTENDED 的数字丢弃而非补救。
- **可归因性**：`collect.sh` 的指纹头（含 commit 的三层回退与 UNKNOWN 即禁发表）、正确性门、PIPESTATUS 失败记账，加上 benchmark.md 的单一 wheel、每型号两台、不一致就都列不平均、未测量就声明未测量——共同保证数字可复现、可比较、可撤回。
- 基准的每个模式是一个**问题**而不是一个数字：stages 问时间去哪了、overlap 问藏了多少、padding/zerocopy 问两条特性路径的代价、sweep 问何时失效、link 问天花板在哪、zerosm 问占不占 SM。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.
